page.layout: Two parts on one page: at top, a block of verse in italic (full width, lines of the epitaph, with running head and page number at top right); below a horizontal rule, then a heading in capitals and a poem of italic verse with a large initial G in the left column.

l.i: Pro quibus intrepidus forte dum fertur in hoste,
Ipse illum Mauors Sidit & obstupuit,
Aggressúsque dolo, & crudelis fraude Veneni,
Sustulit, heu magnis fraus bene nota viris!
Multe tamen Princeps. Nam te Mors ipsa fatetur,
Non aliter Vinci quam potuisse dolo,
Nimirum fieres princeps Pellaus Ut alter,
Consimili decuit te quoque fraude mori.
GAllia felici felix mihi patria nuper,
Idem etiam nuper Rexque paterq; fuit,
Ingenium (nisi me assentatrix turba fefellit)
Cœlesie, & pietis æmula forma Deis:
Iamque mihi externos fors blanda parabat
honores,
Iam poteram magni Cæsaris esse gener:
Quando ferox blanda pro coniuge Parca reper-
ta est,
Quæ mihi pro thalamo fleterneret hunc tu-
mulum, (Vita,
Nec tam erepta mouent tamen hæc me commoda
Quam doleo abruptum nobile pacis opus,
Sed quanquam haud potui pace componere Vrius,
Quis scit ab interitu surget an ipsa meo?

page.notes: Mixed and partly damaged print at the top of the verse; the lines "Sed quanquam", "Vrius" and "Quis scit" are uncertain. The first verse block contains a faint blot. The large initial G is a woodcut letter joined to "Allia".
